overlap_rationale: Four independently trained responsibilities are used: articulated drawer opening, low-clearance block extraction, loaded transport/placement, and loaded drawer closure. Adjacent datasets intentionally overlap on action-supervised intervals in every trajectory: open_drawer/retrieve_tunnel_block share [300,440), 140 actions = 7.0 s per occurrence and 1,680 actions over 12 demonstrations; retrieve_tunnel_block/place_block_in_drawer share [680,840), 160 actions = 8.0 s per occurrence and 1,920 total; place_block_in_drawer/close_drawer share [900,1160), 260 actions = 13.0 s per occurrence and 3,120 total. These spans are much longer than one 8-step execution chunk and cover meaningful approach, final lift/transfer, release, retreat, and handle-approach states. Expected benefit: causal history can be preserved across switches while the receiver has supervised actions for early and late handoffs. Observed evidence is limited to successful executions with object-position variation; it does not prove recovery from unseen contact or placement failures.
